subject: Source-anchored Patterson 2007 / Gainotti 2012 semantic architecture contrast under a constructed fixed-Q,C capacity-identity audit

locators: Semantic dementia section and Box 1, p. 978
source_claims: Both alternatives preserve modality-specific distributed knowledge.
Distributed-only gating versus distributed-plus-hub common convergence are rival explanations.

The reviewed distributed-plus-hub account predicts modality-general impairment after focal hub damage; the reviewed distributed-only alternative does not predict the same pattern from comparable focal disruption.
Clinical semantic dementia is reviewed with generalized deficits and relatively circumscribed anterior temporal degeneration.
Early laterally asymmetric ATL degeneration may show modality-associated impairment.
An interpretation of later bilateral deficits is joint disruption of partly modality-dependent representations rather than loss of a unique amodal hub.

conditional_application.Q: For a candidate pair of systems with routine semantic competence, does an observed representation-produced match support the same type of cross-modal semantic-generalization capacity?
conditional_application.C: Mechanistic dependence on common modality-general convergence versus distributed task-gated pathways for semantic generalization
